subject: Departmental Updates and 5G Small Cell Policy
overview: The Council received operational updates from the Health, Police, and Public Works departments and debated recommendations for an upcoming 5G small cell infrastructure hearing. Members also approved seasonal river recreation permits and addressed resident concerns regarding traffic equipment placement.

items.title: COVID-19 health update
items.summary: Health Director MaryAnn O'Connor reported 264 cases in March and noted that 72% of residents aged 75 and older have received at least one vaccine dose.

items.title: Police Department update and 2020 crime statistics
items.summary: Chief Jack Buckley presented the 2020 crime statistics report highlighting a significant increase in emergency calls, while Detective Brooke Stanton Hurd detailed specialized domestic violence outreach and safety protocols implemented during the pandemic.

items.title: Public Works Department operations update
items.summary: Commissioner Brian Kerins reported on the relaunch of the SeeClickFix platform, the transition of police fleet maintenance to DPW staff, and the resumption of street sweeping on April 1st.

items.title: Routine business and ceremonial resolutions
items.summary: The Council approved a laundry service license and several resolutions including a 70th birthday recognition for Marie Cassidy, the 2021 budget presentation award, and several condolences.

items.title: Main street resident parking concerns
items.summary: The Council referred a resolution to the traffic department seeking a way for residents on main streets to purchase parking permits for adjacent side streets.

items.title: Traffic safety equipment placement
items.summary: The Council referred resident complaints about solar speed traps and crosswalk equipment being installed directly in front of residential doors to the traffic engineer for review.

items.title: Paddle Boston seasonal permit
items.summary: Approved a seasonal permit for Charles River Canoe and Kayak to operate on the Mystic River, with amendments requesting that the administration explore programming partnerships and coordinate river debris removal with the DCR.

items.title: 5G Small Cell Hearing and policy recommendations
items.summary: The Council approved nine recommendations for an upcoming March 31st hearing, including expanding abutter notifications to 500 feet and investigating the impact of cell equipment proximity to residential dwellings.

items.title: Medford Senior Center reopening and outdoor programming
items.summary: Approved a request for a report from the administration regarding plans to safely reopen the Senior Center or provide outdoor recreational programming for seniors.

items.title: Opposition to anti-Asian bigotry and hate crimes
items.summary: The Council approved a resolution standing in solidarity with Asian-Americans and opposing the national increase in anti-Asian violence and white supremacist rhetoric.

items.title: Committee reports and Tufts accountability report
items.summary: Approved reports from the Committee of the Whole regarding a data breach investigation and zoning updates, and received the Tufts University spring 2021 student housing report.
